* feat(reading-stats): centralize help recording + fix position-dependent page stats
This commit bundles the concurrent session's ongoing work on the "reading stats languages and grammar rules" feature (js/selection.js, js/translation.js, js/grammar-svo.js, tests/learning_stats_languages_grammar_browser.py, tests/pdf_sentence_reselect_browser.py, tests/pdf_ux_browser.py, tests/README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md) together with a specific, independently-diagnosed fix in js/learning-stats.js this session was asked to audit for -- both were left interleaved in the shared working tree, the full regression suite passes cleanly with everything combined, and they could not be cleanly separated.
THIS SESSION'S CONTRIBUTION: audited js/learning-stats.js for position-dependent page-statistics counting, per a user report that tapping words near the end of a page, then returning to its beginning, made the statistics appear to "reset" toward 100% independent, as if help given near the bottom stopped counting.
Confirmed the audit's suspicion: tokenIsOnCurrentPage() DID use position-dependent logic for reflowable formats (EPUB/DOCX/TXT/MD -- PDF already always returned true unconditionally). For each candidate word it tested whether its Range's getClientRects() intersected els.container's CURRENT getBoundingClientRect() -- i.e. "is this word inside the live, on-screen viewport right now" -- rather than the reader's own stable, already-tracked state.pageInChapter. Both the denominator (currentPageVocabulary()'s word set) AND which specific occurrences got recorded (recordHelpForSpan() calls currentPageVocabulary() too) went through this same filter.
Confirmed reproducible with a completely realistic trigger: toggling immersive-mode (a normal, frequent UI interaction) changes #reader-container's actual height, and with the old viewport-based check this alone changed a page's total word count (153 -> 142 in one measured run) with zero navigation and zero change to state.pageInChapter. Isolated the exact mechanism cleanly from a SEPARATE, deeper, pre-existing issue found during the same investigation (also confirmed, deliberately NOT fixed here, out of scope for "page statistics logic"): '#reader-pages { height: 100% }' means the browser's own CSS column layout silently re-flows all content across columns whenever the container resizes, independent of state.pageInChapter/totalPagesInChapter -- a pagination/resize-sync issue, not a stats-computation one.
Fix: tokenIsOnCurrentPage() now calls pageIndexForRange() (js/tts.js) -- the SAME stable, computed (not observed) column-index function TTS auto-page-turn already trusts for "which page is this range on" -- and compares it against state.pageInChapter. This has nothing to do with live viewport geometry, so it cannot be affected by scroll position, container size, or the exact instant a check happens to run.
Tests: tests/learning_stats_position_independence_browser.py (new, wired into CI) uses a REAL multi-page markdown document with genuine CSS-column pagination (goToPageInChapter) -- unlike the sibling learning_stats_languages_grammar_browser.py suite's PDF-shaped stub, which always short-circuits true in tokenIsOnCurrentPage() and could never have exercised this path, explaining why the existing suite never caught it. * fix: sync reader pagination/columns with container resize (ResizeObserver)
Root cause: #reader-pages uses height:100%, so the browser's own CSS column layout silently re-flows content whenever #reader-container changes size -- but the only trigger for re-syncing state.pageInChapter/ totalPagesInChapter with that layout was window's 'resize' event. Several real, frequent triggers (immersive-mode toggle, a collapsing sidebar, a mobile browser's dynamic address bar) change the container's actual size through CSS classes alone, with no 'resize' event at all -- so the app's pagination state went silently stale relative to what the browser had already re-flowed to.
Fix: replace the window 'resize' listener with a ResizeObserver on els.container itself -- the one true signal for "this container's rendered box actually changed", regardless of cause. It is a strict superset of the old trigger for this layout: a window resize that changes the container still fires it; one that doesn't (width growth past #reader-container's 900px max-width) correctly triggers nothing. The existing offset-preserving repaginateBook() logic was already correct and is untouched -- only the trigger was unreliable.
Also: a sub-pixel lastContainerResizeSize guard avoids re-triggering on rounding noise across the many intermediate box-size notifications a single CSS transition (.workspace's margin-top/height, 0.3s) fires, and the pre-existing 250ms resizeTimer debounce is kept (same name -- tests/migration_audit_browser.py references it directly).
tests/reader_resize_sync_browser.py: new regression suite. Proves the bug is real (disconnecting the observer reproduces the exact desync -- zero repaginateBook() calls despite a real, measured container resize), then verifies the fix across viewport resize wider/narrower, immersive mode on first/middle/last page, rapid repeated toggling (debounce), resize with an active highlight, resize after recorded help/translation occurrences (verifying the specific records survive, while the page-scoped aggregate is allowed to change since reflow can move words across page boundaries), and resize during active TTS.
tests/pdf_ux_browser.py: its pinch-test setup toggles immersive-mode directly and now correctly triggers the same resize response, which could otherwise land mid-gesture; added a settle-wait before the render-counting checks begin, mirroring the existing pattern in tests/pdf_sentence_reselect_browser.py.
ARCHITECTURE.md updated for both.

* fix: installed PWA shortcut opened a dead address
Root cause: manifest.webmanifest's start_url was "./index.html", which Chrome resolves against the manifest's own URL and bakes verbatim into the installed shortcut (confirmed via Page.getAppManifest: zero installability errors, startUrl exactly ".../index.html"). Cloudflare Pages 308-redirects any literal /index.html request to / (a platform default for files named index.html, not something this repo configures -- no _redirects/_headers file exists here). Once the service worker takes over navigation (every launch after the very first), Chrome refuses to use a Response whose own `.redirected` flag is true to satisfy a navigation's respondWith(), and fails the ENTIRE navigation with net::ERR_FAILED / "this page may have moved to a new address" -- not a JS exception (networkFirstForNavigation() resolved cleanly with a normal 200 Response), a browser-level rule with nothing in the console to point at it. This happens deterministically, online or offline, on every single launch of the shortcut.
Confirmed both contributing paths reproduce it: a live fetch() of that URL (event.request.redirect is forced to 'manual' for navigations, so a redirecting target resolves to an opaqueredirect Response) and, the actual persistent cause, the CACHED copy of './index.html' -- cache.addAll() followed that same redirect at install time, and Cache Storage preserves redirected:true on it forever.
Fix, two parts: - manifest.webmanifest: start_url is now "./" instead of "./index.html". Cloudflare never redirects "/", so no future install ever enters this state. `id` stays "/" (unchanged) so Chrome treats this as an update to the same installed app, not a new one. - sw.js: networkFirstForNavigation() now passes every candidate Response through the new stripRedirectHistory(), which reconstructs a plain `new Response(await res.clone().blob(), {status, statusText, headers})` whenever `.redirected` is true. A freshly-constructed Response has no redirect history, so respondWith() always succeeds -- this heals ANY navigation URL the worker is asked to handle, which is exactly why an ALREADY-installed shortcut -- still permanently pointed at the old "/index.html" start_url -- self-heals the moment the updated worker activates: no reinstall required, confirmed online and offline.
tests/pwa_start_url_browser.py: new regression suite. Runs its own tiny local server (the shared CI one on 8765 doesn't redirect anything) that serves this repo's real files plus the one Cloudflare behavior this bug depends on, so it exercises the actual shipped manifest.webmanifest and sw.js. Traces the full chain via Page.getAppManifest (manifest -> resolved start_url/scope/id -> Chrome's own computed installable manifest) and asserts the URL Chrome would bake into a NEW shortcut resolves with zero redirects. Proves an already-installed shortcut self-heals under the fixed worker, online and offline, while the new start_url also keeps working (no regression). Confirmed (by reverting sw.js/manifest.webmanifest locally and re-running) that the test fails without the fix.
Also: tests/reader_resize_sync_browser.py (added in the previous PR) was never actually wired into .github/workflows/ci.yml despite being recorded as such -- fixed here alongside the new test.
ARCHITECTURE.md updated for both.

* fix: format compatibility audit — HTML title leak, empty TXT, welcome text
Comprehensive audit of every format the app claims to support (traced accept=, extension routing in openBookFile(), FORMAT_SUPPORT.md, and the UI's own "welcome" message against the actual implementation). Confirmed the complete supported list (EPUB, PDF, TXT, DOCX, FB2/FB2.ZIP, MD/ MARKDOWN, HTML/HTM, RTF) is consistent between accept=, routing and FORMAT_SUPPORT.md, but found DOCX/TXT/HTML/HTM/RTF had ZERO automated regression coverage (only FB2/EPUB/Markdown/PDF were tested), and found three confirmed bugs while closing that gap:
1. HTML/HTM title leak + spurious blank first "chapter". Uploading a full saved webpage (the NORMAL shape of a real .html file, not a bare fragment) used to leak its <title> text into visible reader content: initRichDoc()'s HTML branch passed the raw file text straight into safeHtml(), whose allowlist neither renders nor drops <title> -- it falls into the "not a content tag, walk its children" branch, so the title's own text silently became visible content. Because that leaked text sat before the document's first real heading, splitIntoChapters() turned it into an entire separate first "chapter" -- the reader opened directly on a near-blank page showing only the leaked title, with the real content one chapter further in. Fixed in two places: formats.js's HTML/HTM branch now parses the file with DOMParser and keeps only .body.innerHTML (mirroring how loadEpubChapter() already handles real XHTML spine documents, for the identical reason), and core.js's safeHtml() now drops <title> outright as defense in depth.
2. splitIntoChapters() started a new chapter at a heading even when everything accumulated so far was insignificant whitespace (a lone "\n" text node between <body> and its first <h1> -- common in hand-formatted/exported HTML). That produced the spurious blank first chapter independent of bug #1; this fix is the general-purpose correction (a heading now only closes out the previous chapter if it has non-whitespace content).
3. initTxt() had no empty-file guard, unlike every other format's initRichDoc() path -- an empty .txt used to silently "succeed" into a blank single-page reader instead of the same clear emptyDoc error every other unusable file gets. Fixed for consistency.
Also fixed: the UI's own "welcome" message (all 8 interface languages) advertised only "EPUB, PDF or TXT" despite the app supporting DOCX/FB2/ FB2.ZIP/MD/MARKDOWN/HTML/HTM/RTF too -- a real, confirmed mismatch between what the UI claims and what's implemented.
tests/rich_text_formats_browser.py: new regression suite (41 checks) covering the previously-untested DOCX/TXT/HTML/HTM/RTF: import/render/ content (headings, bold/italic, links, embedded images, Ukrainian/ Polish/mixed-language text, punctuation/quotes/apostrophes), TTS extraction order and cleanliness (no HTML/entities leaking into extracted text), reopen/persistence, a representative phone/tablet/ portrait/landscape/immersive-mode viewport matrix (DOCX), and error handling (empty/corrupted/extension-mismatched/unsupported files) across all four formats. DOCX fixtures are minimal hand-built OOXML generated in-memory (no python-docx available; matches this project's existing EPUB/FB2.ZIP fixture convention). Confirmed the title-leak/chapter-split fixes empirically during development and the empty-TXT regression test fails without its fix (reverted locally, re-ran). Full existing suite re-run -- all pass.
Also confirmed (not bugs): extension routing is case-insensitive and compound-extension-aware (.TXT, .Md, .FB2.ZIP all route correctly); filenames with spaces and Ukrainian/Polish characters work correctly; RTF's documented "plain text only, no bold/italic/image" limitation (FORMAT_SUPPORT.md) holds by design; error handling for empty/corrupted/ extension-mismatched/unsupported files was already robust across every format (clear localized message, state fully resets, document.body never left inert, no uncaught JS errors) before this change.

* fix: PDF scanned-image blank-page bug, FB2/EPUB/RTF/TXT format fixes
Deep format/rendering audit covering every supported document format.
## PDF: scanned-image blank page (JPEG2000/JBIG2/CCITT)
Root cause: PDF.js 6 moved JPEG2000/JBIG2/CCITT decoding into separate WASM modules. `pdfjsLib.getDocument({data})` with no `wasmUrl` option silently resolves those image filters to nothing -- render() still resolves successfully, with a completely white, zero-painted-pixel canvas. No error, no warning, no rejected promise: "document loaded, canvas exists, render resolved" all looked fine while the user saw a blank page.
Fix: js/pdf-render.js now passes `wasmUrl` pointing at the vendored decoder assets (vendor/pdfjs-6.3.289/wasm/: openjpeg.wasm, jbig2.wasm, qcms_bg.wasm, plus their pure-JS fallbacks). Verified by reverting the fix and confirming the exact regression (0 painted pixels on a real JPX-encoded PDF; full paint restored with the fix).
Also: getTextContent()/renderTextLayer() failures (damaged text operators) are now isolated in their own try/catch -- an optional text layer must not prevent the page's independent graphical operators from rendering; confirmed a page still paints correctly when text extraction is made to fail.
## Service worker: WASM assets weren't precached for offline
The 5 WASM/fallback files above weren't in sw.js's APP_SHELL. PDF.js's bundled pure-JS decoder means a scan still rendered correctly offline even without them cached (confirmed directly), but every offline scan-PDF open wasted a guaranteed-to-fail network request first before falling back to the slower path. Added all 5 to APP_SHELL; confirmed the WASM fetch now succeeds from the service worker cache offline.
## FB2: cover image silently dropped
FictionBook stores the cover in description/title-info's <coverpage>, outside every <body> -- reading only bodies discarded a legitimate embedded cover. js/formats.js's parseFb2() now also renders the coverpage.
## EPUB: a broken image could blank an entire chapter
No guard existed after safeHtml() for a chapter whose only content was an image that failed to load. Added bookContentPresent() (checks for real text OR a present img[src]/hr) with a clear "image unavailable" error instead of a silent blank page -- and added the imageUnavailable i18n key itself, which was referenced but never defined (users would have seen the literal string "imageUnavailable").
## RTF: text corruption (Ukrainian/Polish/mixed content)
The old parser was a chain of independent regex replacements with no awareness of RTF's actual grouped-scope structure -- \uN/\ucN fallback counts, codepages and ignorable destinations aren't independent of each other. Replaced with a proper tokenizer: {}-scoped state (skip, uc-fallback-count, codepage), correct \'hh codepage-aware byte decoding, \uN Unicode escapes with correct fallback-byte skipping, and ignorable destinations (fonttbl, pict, object, etc.) that never leak into visible text.
## TXT: paragraph selection broken in long files
TXT imports as one <div class="txt-block"> holding the entire file (to preserve source whitespace and character-offset bookmarks) -- paragraphRangeAt() treated that whole div as "the paragraph" whenever tapped, selecting the entire multi-paragraph block instead of one. js/selection.js now detects .txt-block and finds the actual blank-line-delimited paragraph boundaries around the caret.
## CI: cross-suite state-leak fixes
Every *_browser.py suite runs against ONE shared Chrome tab for the whole CI job (.github/workflows/ci.yml). Found and fixed three real leaks between suites, each confirmed by running the entire test sequence in exact CI order on fresh Chrome profiles:
- pdf_rendering_audit_browser.py's device-matrix viewport (and the immersive-mode the app auto-adds below 1180px width, which nothing auto-removes) stayed active after it finished, silently changing how much content fit per page for archive_formats_audit_browser.py immediately after it in the CI sequence. - pwa_start_url_browser.py opened 5 tabs and never closed them (fixed with an atexit-registered cleanup, so a failing check still closes them). - formats_browser.py's font-resize test bumped state.fontSize by 8px and never restored it -- a preference read from localStorage only once, at page-load time, so it silently affected every later suite's pagination math for the rest of the job. - The "image-heavy" EPUB/FB2 fixture (16 images) was never robustly guaranteed to need more than 2 pages at a clean, uncontaminated state -- it only ever passed by riding on the font-size leak above. Bumped to 48 images for a real, measured margin (4 pages).
An explicit Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride (not a clear) is used throughout: this environment's own underlying headless viewport is smaller than any suite assumes, so clearing an override can leave a tab worse off than before.
## Also fixed
.gitignore's blanket `*.pdf`/`*.docx` rule (meant to keep private reading material out of the repo) was also silently excluding this session's own deterministic, redistributable test fixtures -- added narrow exceptions for exactly tests/fixtures/pdf/*.pdf and tests/fixtures/text-audit/*.docx, nothing broader.
tests/ci_suite_coverage.py was added to prevent this class of bug in general: it fails CI if any tests/*_browser.py file isn't explicitly invoked in the workflow.
## Test results
New suites: tests/pdf_rendering_audit_browser.py (real JPX/JBIG2/CCITT/ JPEG codec pixel verification, text-extraction-failure isolation, 3 real producer-generated PDFs with multilingual embedded fonts, 5-device zoom/navigation matrix, malformed/empty/encrypted-input recovery, a 12-cycle memory/DOM-leak stress test), tests/archive_formats_audit_ browser.py (178 checks: EPUB/FB2/FB2.ZIP images/pagination/malformed- input/5-viewport matrix), tests/text_formats_audit_browser.py (179 checks: DOCX/TXT/HTML/MD/RTF corpus incl. CP1250/CP1251/Unicode- fallback RTF edge cases), tests/format_reader_audit_browser.py (323 checks: all 11 extensions x import/render/navigation/selection/ translation/Ask-AI/TTS/stats/reopen x 5 viewports x offline/service- worker/standalone-PWA).
Entire 13-file CI sequence run in exact CI order on fresh Chrome profiles, twice -- fully green both times. Every pre-existing suite (PDF UX, learning stats, language detection, TTS, resize-sync, migration audit) re-run and passing. app_shell_versions.py, browser_cdp_transport.py, ci_suite_coverage.py pass. node --check unavailable in this sandbox (CI covers it); extensive live-browser execution across every changed file is strong evidence it parses correctly. Zero uncaught application errors across the entire run.
## Remaining risk
Real physical Android/iOS device verification (touch latency, GPU compositing, OS memory pressure, real WebAPK install) was not possible in this sandbox -- every mobile/tablet check used CDP viewport/touch emulation, which is not equivalent to a real device.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

<pre style='white-space:pre-wrap;width:81ex'>docs: update HANDOFF.md for PR #84 (PDF word-hitbox stateless fix) (#85)
* lang-detect: detect parenthetical translation pairs independently
In language-learning books a word/phrase is often immediately followed by its translation in parentheses (bonjour (hello), house (maison)). buildLanguageSegments previously classified an entire input string as ONE flat token stream and picked a single base language for it; a single strong anchor anywhere in the string (e.g. "hello") could win that whole-string vote, so a weak-signal word elsewhere (e.g. "bonjour", which never reaches STRONG_MIN) could never be recovered as its own segment even though it resolves correctly when analyzed alone.
Root cause: segment isolation, not a vocabulary gap — "bonjour" analyzed in isolation already resolved to 'fr' via the existing weak-score fallback in sentenceBaseLang.
Fix: split top-level (nesting-aware) parenthesized spans out of the input first and analyze each span independently (buildFlatSegments, the renamed original whole-string algorithm) rather than as part of one flat pass. When a span has no independent strong/weak signal of its own, its tie-break fallback is the language OPPOSITE the immediately preceding real segment (translation-pair semantics) instead of the book's language — this is what recovers "house" (no own signal either way) as English right after French "maison". Plain text outside parentheses keeps its old book-language fallback, since it's a continuation of the sentence, not a translation of it.
Tests: tests/language_paren_browser.py (new, wired into CI) covers both directions (fr->en and en->fr), nested parentheses, a no-own-signal parenthetical, and flat non-parenthetical regression cases. Ran tests/pdf_ux_browser.py, tests/learning_ux_browser.py, tests/migration_audit_browser.py, tests/app_shell_versions.py, and tests/browser_cdp_transport.py locally — all pass.
Also regenerated the content-hash versions (tools/version_app_shell.py) for js/lang-detect.js's changed content in index.html/sw.js.

* lang-detect: context-aware EN/FR clustering for phrases without parens
Language-learning sentences routinely embed a local French word/phrase inside an English sentence (or vice versa) with no parentheses at all: "The French word maison means house.", "Il est très important to pronounce it correctly.", "Comment allez-vous? means How are you?". The previous algorithm required a STRONG opposite-tier token to seed a foreign run and only bridged one neutral "courtesy" neighbor for a multi-word core, so a local phrase with just a weak signal (maison) or an ambiguous cognate with none at all (important, allez-vous) either got swallowed by the sentence's dominant language or split at the wrong boundary.
Root cause, same shape as the parenthesis fix: not enough vocabulary/ signal in isolation, and no mechanism to let a token borrow evidence from its immediate context.
Changes to js/lang-detect.js:
- computeClusters(): one pass groups adjacent same-language word tokens into clusters, bridging up to 2 consecutive neutral (no-signal) tokens as long as the cluster is later reconfirmed by a same-language token (the "1-3 neighboring tokens" context window) — this is what lets "important"/"allez-vous"/"restaurant" ride along with a real anchor instead of needing ad-hoc single-neighbor "courtesy" rules. A real opposite-language token (even weak) always closes the cluster immediately — it's evidence against, not just an absence of evidence. - pickBaseLang(): only clusters with at least one STRONG token vote for the base language (a lone weak-only cluster, e.g. "information"'s "-tion" shape match in an English sentence, never counts — this is the existing false-positive guard, preserved). On a genuine tie between real clusters, the FIRST cluster in reading order wins (a balanced "phrase, then gloss/translation" sentence should keep its opening clause as the base, carving the second as foreign) — falls back to the book language only when there's no real evidence at all, same as before. - findForeignRuns(): now just the base-language's complement among hasStrong clusters — no separate merge step needed since bridging already happens inside computeClusters. - scoreWord(): hyphenated tokens (allez-vous, peut-être — kept as ONE token by LANG_TOKEN_RE) now also check each hyphen-separated part against the word lists, so "vous" inside "allez-vous" is recognized as French even though the whole hyphenated form isn't listed. - FR_COMMON_WORDS/EN_COMMON_WORDS: a small, deliberately short list of common, UNAMBIGUOUS vocabulary beyond closed-class function words (bonjour, merci, maison, bonsoir, salut, madame/monsieur/mademoiselle; English "means" for "X means Y" glosses). Genuinely ambiguous cognates (restaurant, important, menu, table) are intentionally NOT listed — they carry zero own signal and are resolved entirely through the context mechanism above, per the task's own distinction. - debugLanguageSegments(): test-only diagnostic — per-token EN/FR scores and tier, plus resulting segments with character-offset boundaries and the TTS locale each segment resolves to.
buildLanguageSegments' parenthesis handling (splitTopLevelParens/ wrapParenSegments) is untouched; it calls buildFlatSegments per clause exactly as before, which now internally uses the new clustering.

Root cause: buildLanguageLevelPrompt (js/grammar-svo.js) picked the source language via detectLang(sentence || fragment), which detects the DOMINANT language of the whole context sentence "by majority character count." Root cause: js/selection.js's pdfVisualGroup() decided column membership by clustering each individual PDF text FRAGMENT's own left edge. A PDF generator splits a line into a new fragment wherever the style changes mid-sentence (the bold marker word) — that fragment starts deep inside the line, and its own left edge says nothing about which column the whole line belongs to. Pooling every fragment's left edge together let these mid-line values interfere with the real column boundary, fracturing one column's own paragraph into several fake 'columns' (dropping words) or merging it with the other column outright, depending on exact spacing.

* lang-detect: detect parenthetical translation pairs independently
In language-learning books a word/phrase is often immediately followed by its translation in parentheses (bonjour (hello), house (maison)). buildLanguageSegments previously classified an entire input string as ONE flat token stream and picked a single base language for it; a single strong anchor anywhere in the string (e.g. "hello") could win that whole-string vote, so a weak-signal word elsewhere (e.g. "bonjour", which never reaches STRONG_MIN) could never be recovered as its own segment even though it resolves correctly when analyzed alone.
Root cause: segment isolation, not a vocabulary gap — "bonjour" analyzed in isolation already resolved to 'fr' via the existing weak-score fallback in sentenceBaseLang.
Fix: split top-level (nesting-aware) parenthesized spans out of the input first and analyze each span independently (buildFlatSegments, the renamed original whole-string algorithm) rather than as part of one flat pass. When a span has no independent strong/weak signal of its own, its tie-break fallback is the language OPPOSITE the immediately preceding real segment (translation-pair semantics) instead of the book's language — this is what recovers "house" (no own signal either way) as English right after French "maison". Plain text outside parentheses keeps its old book-language fallback, since it's a continuation of the sentence, not a translation of it.
Tests: tests/language_paren_browser.py (new, wired into CI) covers both directions (fr->en and en->fr), nested parentheses, a no-own-signal parenthetical, and flat non-parenthetical regression cases. * lang-detect: context-aware EN/FR clustering for phrases without parens
Language-learning sentences routinely embed a local French word/phrase inside an English sentence (or vice versa) with no parentheses at all: "The French word maison means house.", "Il est très important to pronounce it correctly.", "Comment allez-vous? means How are you?". The previous algorithm required a STRONG opposite-tier token to seed a foreign run and only bridged one neutral "courtesy" neighbor for a multi-word core, so a local phrase with just a weak signal (maison) or an ambiguous cognate with none at all (important, allez-vous) either got swallowed by the sentence's dominant language or split at the wrong boundary.
Root cause, same shape as the parenthesis fix: not enough vocabulary/ signal in isolation, and no mechanism to let a token borrow evidence from its immediate context.
Changes to js/lang-detect.js:
- computeClusters(): one pass groups adjacent same-language word tokens into clusters, bridging up to 2 consecutive neutral (no-signal) tokens as long as the cluster is later reconfirmed by a same-language token (the "1-3 neighboring tokens" context window) — this is what lets "important"/"allez-vous"/"restaurant" ride along with a real anchor instead of needing ad-hoc single-neighbor "courtesy" rules. * lang-detect: detect parenthetical translation pairs independently
In language-learning books a word/phrase is often immediately followed by its translation in parentheses (bonjour (hello), house (maison)). buildLanguageSegments previously classified an entire input string as ONE flat token stream and picked a single base language for it; a single strong anchor anywhere in the string (e.g. "hello") could win that whole-string vote, so a weak-signal word elsewhere (e.g. "bonjour", which never reaches STRONG_MIN) could never be recovered as its own segment even though it resolves correctly when analyzed alone.
Root cause: segment isolation, not a vocabulary gap — "bonjour" analyzed in isolation already resolved to 'fr' via the existing weak-score fallback in sentenceBaseLang.
Fix: split top-level (nesting-aware) parenthesized spans out of the input first and analyze each span independently (buildFlatSegments, the renamed original whole-string algorithm) rather than as part of one flat pass. When a span has no independent strong/weak signal of its own, its tie-break fallback is the language OPPOSITE the immediately preceding real segment (translation-pair semantics) instead of the book's language — this is what recovers "house" (no own signal either way) as English right after French "maison". Plain text outside parentheses keeps its old book-language fallback, since it's a continuation of the sentence, not a translation of it.
Tests: tests/language_paren_browser.py (new, wired into CI) covers both directions (fr->en and en->fr), nested parentheses, a no-own-signal parenthetical, and flat non-parenthetical regression cases. * lang-detect: context-aware EN/FR clustering for phrases without parens
Language-learning sentences routinely embed a local French word/phrase inside an English sentence (or vice versa) with no parentheses at all: "The French word maison means house.", "Il est très important to pronounce it correctly.", "Comment allez-vous? means How are you?". The previous algorithm required a STRONG opposite-tier token to seed a foreign run and only bridged one neutral "courtesy" neighbor for a multi-word core, so a local phrase with just a weak signal (maison) or an ambiguous cognate with none at all (important, allez-vous) either got swallowed by the sentence's dominant language or split at the wrong boundary.
Root cause, same shape as the parenthesis fix: not enough vocabulary/ signal in isolation, and no mechanism to let a token borrow evidence from its immediate context.
Changes to js/lang-detect.js:
- computeClusters(): one pass groups adjacent same-language word tokens into clusters, bridging up to 2 consecutive neutral (no-signal) tokens as long as the cluster is later reconfirmed by a same-language token (the "1-3 neighboring tokens" context window) — this is what lets "important"/"allez-vous"/"restaurant" ride along with a real anchor instead of needing ad-hoc single-neighbor "courtesy" rules. A real opposite-language token (even weak) always closes the cluster immediately — it's evidence against, not just an absence of evidence. - pickBaseLang(): only clusters with at least one STRONG token vote for the base language (a lone weak-only cluster, e.g. "information"'s "-tion" shape match in an English sentence, never counts — this is the existing false-positive guard, preserved). On a genuine tie between real clusters, the FIRST cluster in reading order wins (a balanced "phrase, then gloss/translation" sentence should keep its opening clause as the base, carving the second as foreign) — falls back to the book language only when there's no real evidence at all, same as before. - findForeignRuns(): now just the base-language's complement among hasStrong clusters — no separate merge step needed since bridging already happens inside computeClusters. - scoreWord(): hyphenated tokens (allez-vous, peut-être — kept as ONE token by LANG_TOKEN_RE) now also check each hyphen-separated part against the word lists, so "vous" inside "allez-vous" is recognized as French even though the whole hyphenated form isn't listed. - FR_COMMON_WORDS/EN_COMMON_WORDS: a small, deliberately short list of common, UNAMBIGUOUS vocabulary beyond closed-class function words (bonjour, merci, maison, bonsoir, salut, madame/monsieur/mademoiselle; English "means" for "X means Y" glosses). Genuinely ambiguous cognates (restaurant, important, menu, table) are intentionally NOT listed — they carry zero own signal and are resolved entirely through the context mechanism above, per the task's own distinction. - debugLanguageSegments(): test-only diagnostic — per-token EN/FR scores and tier, plus resulting segments with character-offset boundaries and the TTS locale each segment resolves to.
buildLanguageSegments' parenthesis handling (splitTopLevelParens/ wrapParenSegments) is untouched; it calls buildFlatSegments per clause exactly as before, which now internally uses the new clustering.

User-reported (screenshot: a real bilingual textbook page, French left column / English right column, row-aligned, several sentences with an inline bold marker word — 'Premierement,'/'First,' etc., matching 'Firstly/Secondly/...' style): selecting a sentence grabbed text from BOTH columns at once, and words on the tapped column were sometimes read/detected with the OTHER column's language.
Root cause: js/selection.js's pdfVisualGroup() decided column membership by clustering each individual PDF text FRAGMENT's own left edge. A PDF generator splits a line into a new fragment wherever the style changes mid-sentence (the bold marker word) — that fragment starts deep inside the line, and its own left edge says nothing about which column the whole line belongs to. Pooling every fragment's left edge together let these mid-line values interfere with the real column boundary, fracturing one column's own paragraph into several fake 'columns' (dropping words) or merging it with the other column outright, depending on exact spacing.
A naive 'group by Y first' fix doesn't work either: in a real bilingual layout, the two columns' lines are often at the EXACT same height (translation printed row-for-row opposite the original), so Y-only grouping merges both columns into one row immediately.
Fix: cluster in two stages. First, Y-bands (which CAN span both columns' same-height lines). Then, within each band, sort fragments by X and cut into 'segments' wherever the gap between one fragment's RIGHT edge and the next's LEFT edge exceeds the threshold — a real column gutter, as opposed to a same-line style break where the cursor continues with no real gap. Only each segment's own start-X (not every fragment's) then feeds the existing column-clustering step, so inline style breaks no longer pollute it.

User reported the TTS "echo, doubled with a fraction of a millisecond delay" PERSISTED even after the earlier cancel()->speak() timing fix (tts_double_voice_browser.py / PR #74), and asked to check everything related to speech again.
